outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the building permit application with architectural plans for tenant improvements, including kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, ADA path of travel, and finishes, stamped by a licensed California architect, and request routing to DPH, Planning, SFPUC (FOG), and SFFD. What to say: The plans must show three-compartment sinks, a separate hand-washing sink at each work station, all food-contact surfaces sealed and smooth, the commercial hood and Type I fire suppression system sized for the cooking equipment, the grease interceptor location and size (confirm with SFPUC before submittal), accessible restrooms, and the ADA path from the entrance to all public areas. If the existing occupancy group is B (under 50 people) and the proposed load is 50 or more (A-2), clearly note the change of occupancy on the cover sheet and include an occupant load calculation. Submit the DPH plan check application in parallel, with the menu, equipment list, and scaled kitchen drawings, so plan review runs concurrently.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After DPH plan check approval, schedule a pre-final inspection with the DPH plan reviewer when construction is approximately 80 percent complete, then a final inspection before opening, and submit the health permit to operate application with proof of a certified food safety manager on staff. What to say: Book inspections at least two weeks in advance. Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the final inspection to confirm hand sinks have hot water, all surfaces are sealed, food is stored six inches off the floor, and the hood suppression system has been certified by the installer. The health permit application requires the Business Account Number (BAN), the Location ID (LIN) from DPH, the federal EIN, and the food safety manager certificate. The FY2026–27 application fee is $470 and includes the initial inspection; the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the SFFD place of assembly permit application at the Permit Center (49 South Van Ness, Suite 560) with the approved building plans and the occupant load calculation, and schedule the final fire inspection before the DPH final inspection. What to say: The place of assembly permit fee is $446 for an occupant load of 50 or more. The fire inspector will verify the hood suppression system has been installed and tagged, exit signs and emergency lighting are in place, the maximum occupancy sign is posted, and the path of egress is clear. An undersized or improperly tagged suppression system is a common reason the fire inspection fails, so confirm with the mechanical contractor that the SFFD has signed off on the system before requesting the final inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for background music, and register as an employer with the California EDD and obtain workers' compensation insurance before the first employee is hired. What to say: Federal copyright law requires a blanket ASCAP and BMI license to play recorded music publicly; the two catalogs do not overlap, so both are needed. Annual fees are formula-based on occupancy and run approximately $300–$2,500 per license. Sign up online; licenses are effective immediately. California requires workers' compensation insurance from the first employee, even part-time, and EDD employer registration within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a quarter. Set up payroll and insurance before opening to avoid penalties.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $18,000. Notes: Timeline and cost are for obtaining the Conditional Use Authorization and health permit to operate, if the CUA is required. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days including pre-application meeting, formula retail neighborhood notice (Planning Code Section 311), environmental review, and Planning Commission hearing, followed by a 30-day appeal period. The base CUA fee is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted annually); fees rise with construction cost, and a new storefront business may qualify for a First Year Free fee waiver. The health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for 2026–28) and building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation) run concurrently with the CUA or after it is approved. The eight comparable restaurant agency referrals on this corridor were decided in 7–40 days when no CUA was required. These figures are times to approval when the CUA and health permit are granted; they are not times to a denial or withdrawal. If Planning confirms no CUA is required for this restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change, the timeline compresses to approximately 60–120 days (building permit and health permit only), and government costs drop to approximately $2,300–$17,000 (building, health, fire, sign, and FOG permits). All figures exclude state business registration, food safety certifications, insurance, and music licenses, which are listed separately in the catalog.
